title: reading-notes-llm-neurips-2025-isaac-lee
content:
NeurIPS 2025 - inference notes (focused on systems / kernels / ops)

High-level theme
- Conference had a strong systems tilt this year: many papers focused on end-to-end inference cost (latency + throughput + energy) rather than just model accuracy.
- Two recurring levers: (1) smarter kernel/runtime selection (heterogeneous kernels, adaptive tiling), (2) state/caching optimizations (KV cache eviction, prefix reuse across sessions).
- Several papers provide reproducible microbenchmarks which would be useful to add to our onboard model profiles.

Papers I prioritized
1) "Adaptive Heterogeneous Kernel Selection for Transformer Inference" (NeurIPS 2025)
- Key idea: runtime picks among multiple kernels per op based on input sequence characteristics and hardware utilization, with a lightweight profiler and heatmap-based decision cache.
- Perf: up to 2.1x median p50 token throughput on long-tail sequence mixes vs single best kernel. Lower variance.
- Tradeoffs: switching cost can hurt short-lived sessions; the paper uses a 50ms warmup threshold and amortizes decisions across requests from same user/session.
- Ops implications for Redwood: integrate per-route lightweight profilers, add an LRU decision cache keyed by (model, seq-len-bucket, batch-size, gpu-type). Evaluate switching overhead with continuous-batching.

2) "KV-Cache Attenuation: Memory-aware eviction for multi-tenant LLM serving"
- Key idea: probabilistic attenuation of older KV entries based on estimated reuse likelihood; tackles memory pressure without full recomputation.
- Perf: reduces recompute by ~35% compared to naive FIFO eviction at high tenant counts, with small quality delta on long-context tasks.
- Ops idea: expose attenuation policy knobs per-customer or per-route in Dedicated and Private. Can combine with prefix-hint metadata (client says "this session will use long context").

3) "Quant-inference: Mixed-precision dynamic quantization with calibration-free dequant"
- Key idea: dynamic per-layer quant selection at runtime using a tiny auxiliary model that predicts quantization sensitivity conditioned on the current input distribution. No offline calibration required.
- Perf: shows 1.3-1.6x speedups on A100-ish hardware for 8-bit paths, with smaller degradation than uniform static quant.
- Ops: could be very valuable for Optimize recommendations. But need to measure stability for generative workloads and hallucination risk.

Other notable talks / lightning demos
- A poster demo that combines speculative decoding with early-exit reranking saved ~30% cost for chat-like workloads with low quality drop. This seems promising for interactive customer-facing features.
- Energy-aware scheduling: simple reward functions in scheduler to prefer lower-power instances when latency slack exists. Good fit for cost-optimized Dedicated pools.

Immediate follow-ups (experiments to run at Redwood)
- Kernel switching microbenchmark: reproduce paper's profiler and decision cache. Test with our LLaMA-family and Mistral variants across GPU types (A100, H100, L4). Measure switching overhead with our continuous-batching logic. (owner: Marco)
- KV attenuation prototype: integrate into our prefix/KV cache service as an optional eviction policy; measure end-to-end latency tail under synthetic multi-tenant workloads. Track quality metrics on long-context summarization prompts. (owner: Hannah)
- Dynamic quant path A/B: take one model type and implement the runtime decision proxy to route some requests to dynamic quant path. Monitor output quality (perplexity & targeted eval prompts) and cost. (owner: Isaac)

Notes for product/console integration
- Expose kernel policy traces in Console: per-request kernel choice, decision-cache hit/miss, sequence-length bucket. Useful for debugging perf regressions.
- KV attenuation: provide a slider in Dedicated config: from "conservative" to "aggressive" attenuation with recommended defaults and estimated cost savings.
- For Optimize: add a "dynamic-quant" recommendation type with risk score and sample-based quality estimate.

Open questions / risks
- Stability of dynamic quant on instruction-following and chain-of-thought prompts. Need targeted evals.
- Decision cache privacy: if kernel choice is keyed by customer/session features, ensure no leakage of sensitive session metadata in shared logs.
- Interplay with rollback/fallback: if a kernel switch or quant route causes quality regression, we need automated fallback to a safe path and a mechanism to rollback decision cache entries.

Quick TODO list
- [ ] Kick off kernel-switching microbenchmark ticket (GH #?) and attach NeurIPS paper + author's repo.
- [ ] Add KV-attenuation option to local KV-cache prototype and synthetic tenant runner.
- [ ] Draft short explainer for Console product on dynamic quantization and safety checks.
- [ ] Sync with SRE on observability changes (kernel traces, attenuation metrics) — schedule meeting with SRE and Console.

Useful links / references
- Paper: Adaptive Heterogeneous Kernel Selection - https://neurips.cc/paper/2025/heterogeneous-kernel-selection
- Paper: KV-Cache Attenuation - https://neurips.cc/paper/2025/efficient-kv-cache-attenuation
- Paper: Quant-inference - https://neurips.cc/paper/2025/quant-inference
- Demo repo notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/478

Notes to self
- Keep the microbench harness reproducible: record GPU driver/kernel versions, and provide simple JSON model profiles as input.
- Prioritize tests on L4 (cost-optimized inference GPU) because that's where Optimize recommendations have highest ROI.

End of notes.
